rules.description: The answer treats velocity at the highest point as non-zero instead of momentarily zero.
rules.guidance: Reinforce that the object is momentarily at rest at the highest point, while acceleration due to gravity still acts downward.

rules.description: The answer identifies stopping or zero velocity but misses the role of gravity or acceleration.
rules.guidance: Build on the zero-velocity idea and add that gravitational acceleration continues downward.

rules.description: The answer appears to substitute values into a motion formula without choosing the correct instant or condition.
rules.guidance: Ask the student to identify the condition at the highest point before applying equations.

rules.description: The response gives a memorized formula with little or no conceptual explanation.
rules.guidance: Ask for a one-sentence explanation of why the formula applies.

rules.description: The answer focuses on height, distance, or time when the question asks for velocity.
rules.guidance: Clarify the target quantity in the question before solving.
